liveBlogUpdate.headline: The Norwegian coast guard denies any involvement in the seizure of a ship off Svalbard
liveBlogUpdate.articleBody: The Norwegian coast guard and military were not involved in the seizure of a Russian ship in Svalbard, a coast guard spokesperson stated. This contradicted an earlier report by lawyers involved in the case

liveBlogUpdate.headline: Norway seizes Russian ship in Arctic
liveBlogUpdate.articleBody: A Russian ship has been seized by Norwegian authorities in the Svalbard archipelago. According to Svalbard officials, the seizure was carried out at the request of the Ukrainian state-owned energy company Naftogaz. This follows a previous arbitration ruling that ordered Russia to pay compensation. Moscow is now accusing Norway of piracy. Naftogaz stated that the seizure concerns assets on the Crimean Peninsula, which Russia annexed in 2014. The company owned significant assets there, particularly in the oil and gas sector. The seizure was ordered to enforce outstanding financial obligations to Moscow. Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, according to the state news agency TASS, said that «kidnapping» was a more accurate term for the action

liveBlogUpdate.headline: New rules for air raid alerts in Ukraine
liveBlogUpdate.articleBody: Due to the almost continuous Russian attacks on Kyiv, Ukraine is changing its air raid alert rules. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that a yellow alert level will now be used, for example, when a drone is approaching. A red alert level will signify an attack with ballistic missiles or a massive attack of another kind. Different siren signals will be developed accordingly. Kyiv experienced nine air raid alerts on Wednesday evening. Under these circumstances, public life almost grinds to a halt; businesses cannot operate, and public transportation, especially the metro, is suspended. The main goal of the changes, Zelenskyy wrote on the X platform, is «to give people and businesses in Ukraine more planning certainty and a better understanding of how to react in different situations.»

liveBlogUpdate.headline: Ukraine receives pledges for air defense at EU meeting
liveBlogUpdate.articleBody: Ukraine received new pledges of support for its air defenses at the EU foreign ministers' meeting in Ireland. «We were pleased to hear announcements today from member states that they will provide air defense,» said EU High Representative Kaja Kallas after the conclusion of the talks. This was something that had been requested for a long time. Kallas did not elaborate on who made the new pledges or what they specifically entailed. She said that the member states that had made such announcements would make them public themselves

liveBlogUpdate.headline: Drone found off the coast of Finland
liveBlogUpdate.articleBody: Finnish authorities are investigating the discovery of an unidentified drone off the coast of Porvoo. A possible territorial violation is being considered, according to the German Press Agency (dpa). Police and border guards are investigating the incident, according to Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen. A passerby found the drone on Tuesday. The Ministry of Defense currently believes it to be a surveying drone. No explosives were found, according to the broadcaster Yle. No further information about the circumstances is currently available. Since the outbreak of Russia's war against Ukraine, several Ukrainian drones have repeatedly strayed into the airspace of the Baltic states and some have crashed. In the spring, several Ukrainian drones also reached southeastern Finland

liveBlogUpdate.headline: Ukraine warns against flights over Russia
liveBlogUpdate.articleBody: Ukraine has informed the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) that Russian airspace is unsafe for civil aviation due to increased military activity, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sibiha stated. «We want to prevent unintended incidents,» Sibiha said on the X platform. «War is returning to Russia. Ukraine is exercising its right to self-defense, enshrined in Article 51 of the UN Charter.» The Ukrainian military has repeatedly attacked Russian infrastructure in recent days.

liveBlogUpdate.headline: Poland's Prime Minister: Fire at drone factory was sabotage
liveBlogUpdate.articleBody: The fire at a factory producing combat drones in Poland was caused by sabotage, according to the government. Prime Minister Donald Tusk stated before a cabinet meeting in Warsaw that there was no doubt it was a deliberate act of arson. Tusk added that arson could not be ruled out in another fire at a factory producing components for the aerospace industry in Lublin, but that conclusive evidence was still lacking. On Monday, a fire broke out at the WB Electronics factory in Skarzysko-Kamienna, about 150 kilometers south of Warsaw. No one was injured. The public prosecutor's office is investigating on suspicion of terrorism and working for a foreign intelligence service to the detriment of Poland. According to the radio station RMF.fm, security cameras at the company reportedly show a man wearing a balaclava and carrying a backpack starting a fire in one of the rooms. The intruder also allegedly triggered the alarm system. On Sunday, a fire also broke out at a production and storage facility belonging to the company JFG Composites near Lublin in eastern Poland. The company manufactures components for the aviation industry.

liveBlogUpdate.headline: Putin acknowledges damage to ships caused by Ukrainian attacks
liveBlogUpdate.articleBody: Russian President Vladimir Putin has acknowledged damage to approximately 100 Russian ships caused by Ukrainian drone attacks, according to the German Press Agency (dpa). At the same time, Putin emphasized that Ukraine was not capable of inflicting critical damage on Russia with its attacks. «I think they have caused us real damage,» Putin told reporters on Tuesday in the Kyrgyz capital, Bishkek. «People have died, sailors, including foreign ones,» he said. Citizens of Azerbaijan and Turkey were also among the dead. According to preliminary calculations, the total damage from the attacks currently amounts to one percent of Russia's gross domestic product, Putin said. Ukraine has targeted oil tankers and grain carriers, particularly in the Black Sea and the adjacent Sea of ​​Azov.

liveBlogUpdate.headline: Injuries and damage after Russian attack on Odessa
liveBlogUpdate.articleBody: Russian attacks have damaged infrastructure and residential buildings in the Ukrainian Black Sea port of Odessa, according to a Telegram statement from Sergei Lisak, head of the city's military administration. Eight people were injured, and a 24-story apartment building and several cars were damaged.

liveBlogUpdate.headline: Putin speaks of progress in Ukraine
liveBlogUpdate.articleBody: In the war in Ukraine, Russian troops are advancing ever faster, according to Kremlin chief Vladimir Putin. Russian units have advanced to within a few kilometers of the cities of Sloviansk, Kramatorsk, and Druzhkivka in the Donetsk region, he claimed to representatives of state media in the Kyrgyz capital, Bishkek. The city of Svyatohirsk is once again under Russian control, and street fighting is already taking place in Dobropillia. Putin's claims of successes at the front contradict the assessments of Ukrainian and Western observers, who have recently unanimously noted a slowdown in the Russian advance. In southern Ukraine, according to the Kremlin chief, the Russian army has also advanced to the center of the city of Orikhiv in the Zaporizhzhia region. In northeastern Ukraine, the front line now runs only about twelve kilometers from the regional capital, Sumy, Putin added. In the Kharkiv region of eastern Ukraine, a large group of Ukrainian forces has been encircled on the east bank of the Oskil River. According to Ukrainian and Western observers, there have been few changes on many sections of the front recently. Furthermore, Ukrainian troops have launched successful counterattacks in the eastern Donetsk region near Liman and in southern Ukraine. Russian units have also been largely driven out of the Dnipropetrovsk region
